about.title: Alhambra Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Alhambra sits where several busy routes converge: the I-10 San Bernardino Freeway cuts across the city, while Main Street, Valley Boulevard, and Mission Road carry steady local traffic through its neighborhoods and shopping districts. In 2025, public records show 301 injury collisions inside city limits, 418 people injured, and 2 traffic deaths. Reported crashes in Alhambra tend to cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., when the evening commute and weekend traffic overlap. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the days that follow can feel disorienting. Medical bills arrive, an adjuster from the other driver's insurer calls, and your car may be sitting in a tow yard. LawProactive exists to simplify one part of that. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Alhambra residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened, and we help you reach someone who can review it.

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash to file a lawsuit, but a claim involving a city or state vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. An early connection with an attorney helps keep those deadlines from slipping by.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Close the Door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible for the collision; your share is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. There is also no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case.

items.title: Evidence Fades Fast Along Busy Corridors
items.desc: Business cameras on Main Street or Valley Boulevard may overwrite footage within days, and the other insurer will likely ask for a recorded statement before you have counsel. An attorney can send preservation requests and handle that conversation so you don't have to.

items.question: I was rear-ended on the I-10 near the Alhambra exits. Does it matter that the crash was on a freeway rather than a city street?
items.answer: The legal rules are the same, but the practical details often differ. Freeway crashes are usually handled by the California Highway Patrol rather than Alhambra police, so the report may come from a different agency. Multi-vehicle chain reactions are also more common on the I-10, which can mean several insurers pointing at each other. An attorney can sort out who is responsible and where the report lives.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is generally wise not to before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to minimize your claim. Report the crash to your own insurer as your policy requires, but let counsel handle the other side.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm, and what does it cost?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney; we do not represent you ourselves. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they are paid a percentage of any recovery and nothing if there is none. Using our service costs you nothing at any stage.
